dart2js compile time vs. generated code shape

2026-10-02T05:07:02.468626 · Dart 3.13.5 · macos Version 27.0.1 (Build 26A434) · 10 cores · 238 compiles, N = 1 to 7000

Each point is a single dart compile js -O3 --csp of a generated program with N classes, all instantiated in one main. Variants change one aspect of the generated code; see variants in gen.dart.

Comparing variants: Synthetic ZBase_i classes

Each ZBase_i has an int field plus some combination of ==, hashCode and toString overrides.

  • The parameter type of == makes no meaningful difference: == (dynamic other), == (Object other) and == (Object? other) are within 3.3% of each other at N=7000, which is within the run-to-run noise of a single compile.
  • Overriding == costs 5.24s (1.1×) at N=7000 (== (dynamic other) at 41.5s vs. no == override at 36.2s). The biggest difference is in Enqueue (2.84s, 54% of it), mostly resolution.dynamicUse (2.67s). Scaling goes from N1.90 to N1.83.
  • Adding a hashCode override to a toString override makes little difference at N=7000 (no == override at 36.2s vs. toString only at 34.6s). Scaling goes from N2.00 to N1.90.
  • Adding a toString override to a hashCode override makes little difference at N=7000 (no == override at 36.2s vs. hashCode only at 34.6s). Scaling goes from N1.99 to N1.90.
  • Reading the shared field val inside toString costs 31.1s (10×) at N=7000 (toString only at 34.6s vs. toString only, no field read at 3.45s). The biggest difference is in Enqueue (23.5s, 75% of it), mostly resolution.dynamicUse (23.4s). Scaling goes from N0.90 to N2.00.
  • A toString override that does not read any field costs 883ms (1.3×) at N=7000 (toString only, no field read at 3.45s vs. no overrides at 2.57s). The biggest difference is in kernel loader (191ms, 22% of it). Scaling goes from N0.89 to N0.90.
  • Every class declaring a field with the same name (vs. unique names) costs 30.0s (3.6×) at N=7000 (== (dynamic other) at 41.5s vs. == (dynamic other), unique field names at 11.5s). The biggest difference is in Enqueue (25.4s, 85% of it), mostly resolution.dynamicUse (25.5s). Scaling goes from N1.12 to N1.83.
  • Declaring val on every subclass (vs. once on the base class) costs 32.9s (4.8×) at N=7000 (== (dynamic other) at 41.5s vs. == (dynamic other), field on base class at 8.60s). The biggest difference is in Enqueue (25.6s, 78% of it), mostly resolution.dynamicUse (25.5s). Scaling goes from N0.99 to N1.83.
  • All N inserts in one giant main (vs. helpers of 100 statements) costs 25.9s (2.7×) at N=7000 (== (dynamic other) at 41.5s vs. == (dynamic other), main split up at 15.6s). The biggest difference is in Enqueue (25.4s, 98% of it), mostly resolution.dynamicUse (25.4s). Scaling goes from N1.29 to N1.83.
  • A giant main once field names are unique makes little difference at N=7000 (== (dynamic other), unique field names at 11.5s vs. unique field names + main split up at 11.5s). Scaling goes from N1.12 to N1.12.
  • All classes in one library (vs. a library per class, same public field name) saves 3.44s (1.1×) at N=7000 (== (dynamic other) at 41.5s vs. == (dynamic other), library per class at 44.9s). The biggest difference is in kernel loader (2.17s, 63% of it). Scaling goes from N1.72 to N1.83.
  • A public field name shared across libraries (vs. a private _val per library) costs 25.8s (2.4×) at N=7000 (== (dynamic other), library per class at 44.9s vs. == (dynamic other), library per class, private _val at 19.1s). The biggest difference is in Enqueue (20.1s, 78% of it), mostly resolution.dynamicUse (20.2s). Scaling goes from N1.22 to N1.72.

Breakdown for == (dynamic other)

  • Compile time went from 336ms at N=1 to 41.5s at N=7000, 123× slower for 7000× more classes. From N=1750 up it scales as roughly N1.83 (about quadratic).
  • Most of the extra time comes from Enqueue (+26.1s, 63% of the increase), SSA builder (+6.07s, 15% of the increase) and SSA optimizer (+3.33s, 8.1% of the increase).
  • Fastest-growing phases that take at least 5% of the time at N=7000: Enqueue > resolution.dynamicUse (N2.55, 62% of the time), Enqueue (N2.47, 63% of the time) and SSA builder (N1.70, 15% of the time). These grow faster than the total, so they will dominate even more at larger N.
  • Between N=100 and N=7000, Enqueue grew from 5.2% to 63% of compile time, while kernel loader fell from 36% to 3.5%.
  • The amount of work dart2js reports grows at most as N0.98 (about 40 inferred types per class), but time grows as N1.83. The cost per element is rising with program size, which points at non-linear behavior inside the phases above rather than just more code to compile.
  • Outside the compiler itself (VM startup, make), each compile costs a roughly fixed 97ms of wall-clock time on average.

  • Fastest-growing phases that take at least 5% of the time at N=7000: Enqueue > resolution.dynamicUse (N2.55, 61% of the time), Enqueue (N2.47, 62% of the time) and SSA builder (N1.74, 15% of the time). These grow faster than the total, so they will dominate even more at larger N.
  • Between N=100 and N=7000, Enqueue grew from 4.9% to 62% of compile time, while kernel loader fell from 35% to 3.4%.
  • The amount of work dart2js reports grows at most as N0.98 (about 40 inferred types per class), but time grows as N1.85. The cost per element is rising with program size, which points at non-linear behavior inside the phases above rather than just more code to compile.
  • Outside the compiler itself (VM startup, make), each compile costs a roughly fixed 98ms of wall-clock time on average.

Breakdown for toString only

  • Compile time went from 336ms at N=1 to 34.6s at N=7000, 103× slower for 7000× more classes. From N=1750 up it scales as roughly N2.00 (about quadratic).
  • Most of the extra time comes from Enqueue (+23.7s, 69% of the increase), SSA builder (+5.19s, 15% of the increase) and SSA optimizer (+2.49s, 7.3% of the increase).
  • Fastest-growing phases that take at least 5% of the time at N=7000: Enqueue > resolution.dynamicUse (N2.47, 68% of the time), Enqueue (N2.43, 68% of the time) and SSA builder (N1.84, 15% of the time). These grow faster than the total, so they will dominate even more at larger N.
  • Between N=100 and N=7000, Enqueue grew from 3.9% to 68% of compile time, while kernel loader fell from 37% to 2.2%.
  • The amount of work dart2js reports grows at most as N0.96 (about 10 inferred types per class), but time grows as N2.00. The cost per element is rising with program size, which points at non-linear behavior inside the phases above rather than just more code to compile.
  • Outside the compiler itself (VM startup, make), each compile costs a roughly fixed 100ms of wall-clock time on average.

Breakdown for == (dynamic other), library per class

  • Compile time went from 346ms at N=1 to 44.9s at N=7000, 130× slower for 7000× more classes. From N=1750 up it scales as roughly N1.72 (about quadratic).
  • Most of the extra time comes from Enqueue (+26.5s, 60% of the increase), SSA builder (+6.45s, 14% of the increase) and kernel loader (+3.46s, 7.8% of the increase).
  • Fastest-growing phases that take at least 5% of the time at N=7000: Enqueue > resolution.dynamicUse (N2.24, 58% of the time), Enqueue (N2.19, 59% of the time) and SSA builder (N1.77, 14% of the time). These grow faster than the total, so they will dominate even more at larger N.
  • Between N=100 and N=7000, Enqueue grew from 3.7% to 59% of compile time, while kernel loader fell from 50% to 8.0%.
  • The amount of work dart2js reports grows at most as N0.98 (about 40 inferred types per class), but time grows as N1.72. The cost per element is rising with program size, which points at non-linear behavior inside the phases above rather than just more code to compile.
  • Outside the compiler itself (VM startup, make), each compile costs a roughly fixed 125ms of wall-clock time on average.
